title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 8 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Chronicles chapter 8 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 8 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Chronicles Chapter 8.

questions.question: Who was the firstborn son of Benjamin according to 1 Chronicles 8?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:1 states that Benjamin begat Bela his firstborn.

questions.question: Which of these was NOT one of Bela's sons?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:3 lists Bela's sons as Addar, Gera, and Abihud. Ashbel was a son of Benjamin, not Bela.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 8, who were the sons of Elpaal?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:12 states the sons of Elpaal were Eber, Misham, and Shamed.

questions.question: True or False: Ehud was one of the heads of the fathers of the inhabitants of Geba.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:6 says these are the sons of Ehud, who were heads of the fathers of the inhabitants of Geba.

questions.question: Who was sent away and begat children in the country of Moab?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:8 states that Shaharaim begat children in the country of Moab after he had sent them away.

questions.question: Which wives did Shaharaim have according to 1 Chronicles 8?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:8 mentions that Hushim and Baara were Shaharaim's wives.

questions.question: True or False: Jobab was a son of Hodesh, wife of Shaharaim.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:9 states that Shaharaim begat Jobab of Hodesh his wife.

questions.question: Which city did Shamed, son of Elpaal, build?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:12 states Shamed, son of Elpaal, built Ono and Lod.

questions.question: Who were the heads of the fathers of the inhabitants of Aijalon?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:13 states Beriah and Shema were heads of the fathers of the inhabitants of Aijalon.

questions.question: True or False: The inhabitants of Aijalon drove away the inhabitants of Gath.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:13 states that the inhabitants of Aijalon, led by Beriah and Shema, drove away the inhabitants of Gath.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT listed as a son of Beriah?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:16 lists Michael, Ispah, and Joha as sons of Beriah. Ahaz is from another lineage.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 8, who was removed and begat Uzza and Ahihud?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:7 mentions Naaman, Ahiah, and Gera were removed, and Gera begat Uzza and Ahihud.

questions.question: True or False: The heads of the fathers mentioned in 1 Chronicles 8:28 dwelt in Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:28 states that these chief men dwelt in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which of these names is listed as a son of Shimhi?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:21 names Adaiah as one of the sons of Shimhi.

questions.question: In 1 Chronicles 8, which event comes first?
options: The sons of Elpaal built Ono and Lod
Beriah and Shema drove away the inhabitants of Gath
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:1 mentions Benjamin begat Bela first, which is earlier than the other events listed in subsequent verses.

medium.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 8 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Chronicles Chapter 8 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Which three sons of Beriah are mentioned in 1 Chronicles 8:16?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:16 specifically lists Michael, Ispah, and Joha as the sons of Beriah, distinguishing them from other sons mentioned in adjacent verses.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 8:17, who are listed as sons of Beriah alongside Zebadiah?
questions.explanation: Verse 17 names Meshullam, Hezeki, and Heber as sons of Beriah along with Zebadiah, showing the family's breadth.

questions.question: What can we learn about faithfulness and family legacy from the listing of Elpaal’s sons in 1 Chronicles 8:18?
options: Ishmerai, Jezliah, and Jobab carried on the family line
Elpaal had no sons to continue his legacy
Only one son of Elpaal is mentioned
Elpaal’s sons were separated from the community
questions.correctAnswer: Ishmerai, Jezliah, and Jobab carried on the family line
questions.explanation: Verse 18 shows that Elpaal had multiple sons— I shmerai, Jezliah, and Jobab—highlighting the importance of family continuity and faithfulness in God’s plan.

questions.question: Which sons of Shimhi are named in 1 Chronicles 8:21?
questions.explanation: Verse 21 clearly names Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath as the sons of Shimhi, indicating their role as heads of families.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 8:28 describe the leaders mentioned in the preceding verses, and what does this imply about their role?
options: They were chief men and heads of fathers dwelling in Jerusalem
They were common citizens scattered in various towns
They were priests serving at the temple
They were exiles living outside Judah
questions.correctAnswer: They were chief men and heads of fathers dwelling in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Verse 28 calls these men 'heads of the fathers' and 'chief men' who lived in Jerusalem, emphasizing their leadership and responsibility within the community (verses 15-27).

questions.question: True or False: 1 Chronicles 8:27 lists Jeroham's sons as Jaresiah, Eliah, and Zichri.
questions.explanation: Verse 27 clearly names Jaresiah, Eliah, and Zichri as sons of Jeroham, confirming the accuracy of the statement.

questions.question: What lesson about integrity and leadership can be drawn from the detailed genealogies of heads of families in 1 Chronicles 8:15-28?
options: Leadership requires a faithful lineage and recognition of God’s order
Leadership is based on wealth and power exclusively
Only priests can lead the people
questions.correctAnswer: Leadership requires a faithful lineage and recognition of God’s order
questions.explanation: The passage highlights heads of families chosen from established lineages, indicating that faithful family heritage and God’s appointment are essential for leadership (verses 15-28).

questions.question: According to verses 19 and 20, which of the following groups are sons of Elpaal and Shimhi respectively?
options: Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi; Adaiah, Beraiah, Shimrath
Abdon, Zichri, Hanan; Zebadiah, Arad, Ader
Elienai, Zilthai, Eliel; Ishpan, Heber, Eliel
Michael, Ispah, Joha; Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah
questions.correctAnswer: Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi; Adaiah, Beraiah, Shimrath
questions.explanation: Verse 19 lists Jakim, Zichri, and Zabdi as sons of Elpaal, while verse 21 identifies Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath as sons of Shimhi, helping us understand family relationships.

questions.question: True or False: The passage in 1 Chronicles 8:25-26 includes the sons of Jeroham as Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah, Jaresiah, Eliah, and Zichri.
questions.explanation: Verses 25-26 mention Shamsherai, Shehariah, and Athaliah as sons of Shashak, while verse 27 lists Jaresiah, Eliah, and Zichri as sons of Jeroham. The two groups come from different fathers.

questions.question: What practical Christian virtue is demonstrated by the heads of the fathers dwelling together in Jerusalem as noted in 1 Chronicles 8:28?
questions.explanation: Verse 28 emphasizes that these chief men lived together in Jerusalem, modeling unity and shared responsibility within the faith community.

questions.question: Based on 1 Chronicles 8:22-23, which pairs of sons belong to Ishpan and Abdon respectively?
options: Ishpan, Heber, Eliel; Abdon, Zichri, Hanan
Abdon, Zichri, Hanan; Ishpan, Heber, Eliel
Zebadiah, Arad, Ader; Michael, Ispah, Joha
Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi; Elienai, Zilthai, Eliel
questions.correctAnswer: Ishpan, Heber, Eliel; Abdon, Zichri, Hanan
questions.explanation: Verse 22 lists Ishpan, Heber, and Eliel as sons of Shimhi, while verse 23 names Abdon, Zichri, and Hanan as sons of Shimhi's family, clarifying family lines.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 8:15-16 illustrate the importance of diversity within a community of faith?
options: By showing a variety of sons with different names and roles in one family line
By emphasizing that only one person leads
By highlighting the exclusion of some families
By focusing only on priests and Levites
questions.correctAnswer: By showing a variety of sons with different names and roles in one family line
questions.explanation: Verses 15-16 list multiple sons of Beriah with distinct names, demonstrating how a community benefits from varied individuals working together.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 8:24, Antothijah is listed as a son of Shashak.
questions.explanation: Verse 24 lists Antothijah as a son of Jeroham, not Shashak. Shashak's sons are mentioned in verse 25 instead.

questions.question: Which of the following best illustrates the biblical virtue of humility as seen in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 8:15-28?
options: Acknowledging the contributions of each family member in the community
Separating oneself from others to gain status
questions.correctAnswer: Acknowledging the contributions of each family member in the community
questions.explanation: The detailed listing of family heads shows respect and acknowledgment of all members, teaching humility and collective honor (verses 15-28).

questions.question: How can the record of chiefs dwelling in Jerusalem in 1 Chronicles 8:28 encourage a believer struggling with isolation?
options: It shows the importance of community and belonging within the faith
It suggests being alone is preferable for spiritual growth
It encourages leaving the city to find solitude
It prioritizes political power over fellowship
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the importance of community and belonging within the faith
questions.explanation: Verse 28 emphasizes that leaders lived together in Jerusalem, encouraging believers to seek fellowship and support rather than isolation.

hard.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 8 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Chronicles Chapter 8.

questions.question: Who was the wife of the father of Gibeon according to 1 Chronicles 8?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:29 states that the father of Gibeon had a wife named Maachah.

questions.question: Which son of the father of Gibeon was his firstborn?
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 8:30, Abdon was the firstborn son of the father of Gibeon.

questions.question: Where did Mikloth and his descendants dwell according to 1 Chronicles 8?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:32 says Mikloth begat Shimeah, and they dwelt with their brethren in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Who was the father of Saul according to 1 Chronicles 8?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:33 states that Ner begat Kish, and Kish begat Saul.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of Saul's sons listed in 1 Chronicles 8?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:33 lists Saul's sons as Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal. Shimeah was a son of Mikloth (verse 32).

questions.question: Who was the son of Jonathan mentioned in 1 Chronicles 8?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:34 states that the son of Jonathan was Meribbaal.

questions.question: Which of these was NOT a son of Micah according to 1 Chronicles 8?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:35 lists Micah's sons as Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz. Binea was a son of Moza (verse 37).

questions.question: Who begat Jehoadah according to 1 Chronicles 8?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:36 states Ahaz begat Jehoadah.

questions.question: How many sons did Azel have, and can you name one?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:38 mentions Azel had six sons, including Azrikam.

questions.question: What notable characteristic is given about the sons of Ulam in 1 Chronicles 8?
options: Mighty men of valour and archers
questions.correctAnswer: Mighty men of valour and archers
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:40 describes the sons of Ulam as mighty men of valour and archers.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 8, Kish was a descendant of Ner.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:33 states Ner begat Kish, so Kish was a descendant of Ner.

questions.question: True or False: The sons of Eshek included Azel and Bocheru according to 1 Chronicles 8.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:39 and 8:38 show that Azel and Bocheru were sons of Azel, who was descended from Moza, not sons of Eshek. Eshek’s sons were Ulam, Jehush, and Eliphelet.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage shares the theme of Saul’s lineage as presented in 1 Chronicles 8:33?
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9 introduces Saul, son of Kish, paralleling 1 Chronicles 8:33 which traces Saul’s genealogy.

questions.question: What is the significance of the name 'Meribbaal' mentioned in 1 Chronicles 8:34, and which New Testament passage indirectly reflects on this lineage?
options: It means 'contender with Baal'; reflected in Acts 13:22 where Saul is called a man after God's own heart
It means 'mighty warrior'; reflected in Ephesians 6:10
questions.correctAnswer: It means 'contender with Baal'; reflected in Acts 13:22 where Saul is called a man after God's own heart
questions.explanation: Meribbaal means 'contender with Baal'; Acts 13:22 refers to Saul as a man after God's own heart, showing contrast and fulfillment of God's plan through this lineage.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 1 Chronicles 8 when listing genealogies, as seen especially from verses 29 to 40?
questions.explanation: The genealogical lists create an inclusio structure framing the lineage from the father of Gibeon to the mighty men of Benjamin, emphasizing continuity and identity (verses 29-40).

theological.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 8 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Chronicles Chapter 8 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which of Benjamin's sons is identified as his firstborn in 1 Chronicles 8?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:1 explicitly states that Bela was Benjamin's firstborn son.

questions.question: What theological doctrine can be drawn from the detailed genealogies of Benjamin’s descendants in 1 Chronicles 8:3-5?
options: Doctrine of Divine Providence in preserving the lineage
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of Divine Providence in preserving the lineage
questions.explanation: The genealogy in 1 Chronicles 8:3-5 shows God's providential preservation of the tribe of Benjamin, emphasizing His sovereign hand in maintaining His covenant people’s lineage, which aligns with the doctrine of Divine Providence.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 8:6-7, what role did Ehud’s sons have among the inhabitants of Geba?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states that the sons of Ehud were 'heads of the fathers' of the inhabitants of Geba, indicating leadership roles in their community.

questions.question: What does the mention of Shaharaim’s marriages in Moab in 1 Chronicles 8:8 teach about Israel's history?
options: Israel’s interactions and intermarriages with neighboring nations
The exclusive holiness of Israel’s lineage
The rejection of foreign wives by Israel
The establishment of Moab as Israel’s capital
questions.correctAnswer: Israel’s interactions and intermarriages with neighboring nations
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 8:8 notes Shaharaim begat children in Moab and had Moabite wives, reflecting Israel’s complex historical relationships and intermarriages with neighboring peoples.

questions.question: Which city did the sons of Elpaal build according to 1 Chronicles 8:12?
questions.explanation: Verse 12 clearly states that the sons of Elpaal built Ono and Lod, including the towns thereof.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth is taught by 1 Chronicles 8:13 and 8:16 regarding leadership and spiritual authority?
options: God appoints specific heads who lead in spiritual and military roles
All leadership is based on hereditary monarchy alone
Spiritual authority is separate from tribal leadership
Leadership is only established after the exile
questions.correctAnswer: God appoints specific heads who lead in spiritual and military roles
questions.explanation: Verses 13 and 16 identify Beriah and his sons as 'heads of the fathers' and chief men, implying divinely appointed leadership with both spiritual and military responsibilities.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 8:28 contribute to the biblical narrative of God’s covenant people dwelling in Jerusalem?
options: It confirms the Benjaminite chiefs dwelt in Jerusalem, highlighting the city's centrality
It indicates Jerusalem was abandoned at that time
It shows that Benjaminites were exiled away from Jerusalem
It notes that Jerusalem was a foreign city for Benjamin
questions.correctAnswer: It confirms the Benjaminite chiefs dwelt in Jerusalem, highlighting the city's centrality
questions.explanation: Verse 28 notes that these chief men from Benjamin dwelt in Jerusalem, emphasizing Jerusalem’s role as the spiritual and political center for God's covenant people.

questions.question: What attribute of God is reflected in the preservation of Saul’s genealogy in 1 Chronicles 8:33?
options: God’s faithfulness in preserving His chosen king’s lineage
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness in preserving His chosen king’s lineage
questions.explanation: Verse 33 traces Saul’s genealogy, indicating God’s faithfulness in preserving the lineage of the first king of Israel, part of His covenantal plan for redemption.

questions.question: Which doctrinal theme emerges from the genealogy of Jonathan's son Meribbaal and his descendants in 1 Chronicles 8:34-36?
options: The continuity of covenant blessings through generations
The doctrine of sanctification by works
The cessation of the Davidic line
questions.correctAnswer: The continuity of covenant blessings through generations
questions.explanation: Verses 34-36 show the continuation of Jonathan’s descendants, symbolizing God’s ongoing covenant blessings and promises through successive generations.

questions.question: What combined teaching do 1 Chronicles 8:37-38 and 8:39-40 convey about God’s provision for strength and valor in His people?
options: God raises mighty men of valor within His covenant community
God rejects all physical strength in favor of spiritual gifts
Only Levites possess valor and strength
Valor is unrelated to God’s providence
questions.correctAnswer: God raises mighty men of valor within His covenant community
questions.explanation: These verses list descendants known for valor and strength, showing God’s provision of physical and military strength to His people as part of His covenant care.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the detailed genealogies in 1 Chronicles 8 are irrelevant to understanding God’s plan of salvation. What does 1 Chronicles 8:1-40 actually teach about God’s redemptive plan?
options: Genealogies demonstrate God’s faithfulness in preserving His covenant people and foreshadow Christ’s lineage
Genealogies are mere historical records with no spiritual significance
Genealogies prove that only Israel is saved
Genealogies show God’s rejection of Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: Genealogies demonstrate God’s faithfulness in preserving His covenant people and foreshadow Christ’s lineage
questions.explanation: The genealogies in 1 Chronicles 8 establish the preservation of God’s covenant people, ultimately leading to the Messiah’s lineage in the tribe of Benjamin (cf. Romans 11:1). This underscores God’s providence and redemptive plan.

questions.question: Which doctrinal truth is highlighted by the repeated mention of 'heads of the fathers' in 1 Chronicles 8:6, 13, and 27?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'heads of the fathers' indicates God’s establishment of structured leadership within His people, reflecting the doctrine of divinely ordained authority and governance.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 8:29-31 illustrate God’s providential care in preserving the family lines critical for Israel’s future?
options: By naming the father of Gibeon and his sons, it shows God’s attention to family continuity
It shows God’s rejection of Gibeon’s family
It reveals the destruction of Gibeon
It teaches that only Jerusalem families are important
questions.correctAnswer: By naming the father of Gibeon and his sons, it shows God’s attention to family continuity
questions.explanation: The detailed listing of the father of Gibeon and his sons highlights God’s providential care in preserving key family lines vital for Israel’s stability and covenantal identity.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated in 1 Chronicles 8:22-23 through the preservation of the sons of Shimhi and their descendants?
options: God’s faithfulness to His covenant promises
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness to His covenant promises
questions.explanation: The preservation of Shimhi’s sons and their descendants illustrates God’s faithfulness in maintaining His covenant promises to His people, ensuring their ongoing identity and blessing.

questions.question: What narrative arc is advanced by 1 Chronicles 8:32-33 concerning the rise of Saul?
options: The establishment of Israel’s monarchy through God’s chosen king
The end of the tribal confederacy system
The rejection of the tribe of Benjamin
questions.correctAnswer: The establishment of Israel’s monarchy through God’s chosen king
questions.explanation: These verses trace Saul’s genealogy, marking the rise of the monarchy and God’s sovereign choice of Saul as the first king, advancing the biblical narrative of redemption.
